description_summary: 12-month unduplicated enrollment headcounts broken down by enrollment level, sex, and nine race/ethnicity categories. Each record is uniquely identified by UNITID and EFFYLEV (enrollment level), and includes undergraduate and graduate levels.

12-month instructional activity totals measured in credit hours and/or contact hours, reported by instructional level for undergraduate and graduate activity. The table contains institution-level activity records rather than student headcounts; its distinguishing measures are total credit-hour and contact-hour activity used for 12-month FTE calculations.

Institution-level academic library records for 2011-12, covering library characteristics, collections, expenditures, and services; this is a subset of the 2011-12 Academic Library survey variables retained for comparability with IPEDS data collected from 2014-15 onward. The table applies only to degree-granting institutions, with expenditure fields available only for institutions reporting total expenditures over $100,000.

Awards and degrees conferred by six-digit CIP program, first or second major, award level, race/ethnicity, and gender. Each record is uniquely identified by UNITID, CIPCODE, MAJORNUM, and AWLEVEL, and contains award totals plus gender and race/ethnicity breakdowns.

Students receiving any degree or certificate, broken down by race/ethnicity and gender. There is one record per institution, uniquely identified by UNITID; this table counts students rather than individual awards and has no program or award-level detail.

Students receiving degrees or certificates by award level, race/ethnicity, gender, and age category. Each record is uniquely identified by UNITID and AWLEVEL; age groups are under 18, 18–24, 25–39, and 40 or older, but race, gender, and age are not available in combination.

Programs offered and programs offered via distance education by CIP program and award level. Each record is uniquely identified by UNITID and CIPCODE: six-digit CIP records show award-level offerings and distance-education status, two-digit CIP records summarize the number of six-digit programs in the group, and CIPCODE 99 provides institution totals.

Fall enrollment counts broken down by gender, full- or part-time attendance status, and student level. Each record is uniquely identified by UNITID and EFLEVEL, which combines attendance status and level; measures include total enrollment and male/female counts.

Fall enrollment counts broken down by race/ethnicity, gender, full- or part-time attendance status, and student level, with all nine race/ethnicity categories. Each record is uniquely identified by UNITID and EFALEVEL, which combines attendance status and level; measures include total enrollment and male/female counts.

Fall enrollment counts broken down by distance-education status and student level. Each record is uniquely identified by UNITID and EFDELEV; measures distinguish students enrolled exclusively, partly, or not at all in distance education, and exclusively distance-education students are further classified by location: same state/jurisdiction, another state/jurisdiction, U.S. location unknown, or outside the U.S.

Fall enrollment counts broken down by age category, gender, full- or part-time attendance status, and student level. Each record is uniquely identified by UNITID, EFBAGE, and LSTUDY. Age enrollment reporting is optional in even-numbered years, so 2012 (even) has data, but coverage is institutionally incomplete.

First-time freshman counts broken down by state of residence, including counts who graduated from high school the previous year. Each record is uniquely identified by UNITID and EFCSTATE. Residence enrollment reporting is optional in odd-numbered years, so 2012 (even) is not an optional year and has data.

Fall enrollment counts in selected major fields—Education, Engineering, Biological/Life Sciences, Mathematics, Physical Sciences, Business, Law, Dentistry, and Medicine—broken down by race/ethnicity, gender, full- or part-time attendance status, and student level. This table is restricted to four-year institutions; each record is uniquely identified by UNITID, major field of study, and EFCIPLEV.

Institution-level measures of total entering class, first-year retention rate, and student-to-faculty ratio for institutions with undergraduate students. Entering-class data are available only for academic-year institutions; short-program institutions of less than one year do not have retention data. The table has one institution-level record identified by UNITID.

Institution-level finance data for public institutions using GASB 34/35 accounting standards, including revenues by source, expenditures by category, assets, and liabilities. Each record is unique by institution.

Institution-level finance data for private not-for-profit institutions and public institutions using FASB accounting standards, including revenues by source, expenditures by category, assets, and liabilities. Each record is unique by institution; it excludes public institutions reporting under GASB and private for-profit institutions.

Institution-level finance data for private for-profit institutions using FASB accounting standards, including revenues by source, expenditures by category, assets, and liabilities. Each record is unique by institution; it excludes public institutions and private not-for-profit institutions.

Graduation and completion counts at 100%, 150%, and 200% of normal time, with no transfer outcome specified, for 4-year institutions’ 2004 bachelor’s-seeking cohorts and less-than-4-year institutions’ 2008 full-time, first-time cohorts. The 4-year population is restricted to bachelor’s degree-seeking students, while the less-than-4-year population covers students seeking any degree or certificate.

Graduation, completion, and transfer counts at 150% of normal time for 4-year institutions’ 2006 cohorts and 2-year institutions’ 2009 cohorts, broken down by gender and race/ethnicity. Records are uniquely defined by IPEDS ID (UNITID), cohort and graduation status (GRTYPE); the table includes bachelor’s-seeking and other degree/certificate-seeking cohorts at 4-year institutions and full-time first-time cohorts at 2-year institutions. For 2-year institutions, 100%-of-normal-time completion counts are not available by gender and race/ethnicity.

Graduation, completion, and transfer counts at 100% and 150% of normal time for the 2009 cohort at less-than-2-year institutions. The population is restricted to full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates; it includes cohort enrollment and outcomes but no gender or race/ethnicity breakdown is specified.

Staff counts broken down by full- or part-time status, medical-school status, occupational category, tenure status, and—where applicable—contract type. Each row is uniquely identified by UNITID and EAPCAT, which combines occupational category and tenure status.

Counts of full-time instructional staff at degree-granting institutions with 15 or more full-time employees and related administrative offices, broken down by faculty and tenure status, academic rank, race/ethnicity, gender, and contract type. Each row is uniquely identified by UNITID and SISCAT, which combines faculty/tenure status with academic rank. Race/ethnicity and gender reporting is optional in even-numbered years, so 2012 (even) does not have data for all institutions.

Full-time new-hire counts at degree-granting institutions with 15 or more full-time employees and related administrative offices, broken down by primary occupational category, race/ethnicity, gender, and, for instructional occupations, faculty/tenure status. Each row is uniquely identified by UNITID and SNHCAT, which defines the occupation and instructional faculty/tenure category. Human Resources reporting is optional in even-numbered years, so 2012 (even) does not have data for all institutions.

Full- and part-time payroll staff counts broken down by occupational category, race/ethnicity, and gender. Each row is uniquely identified by UNITID and STAFFCAT, which combines occupational category with full- or part-time status. Race/ethnicity and gender reporting is optional in even-numbered years, so 2012 (even) does not have data for all institutions.

Counts of full-time instructional staff at degree-granting institutions with 15 or more full-time employees and related administrative offices, broken down by academic rank, faculty status, tenure status, and contract type. Each row is uniquely identified by UNITID and FACSTAT, the faculty/tenure-status category.

Full-time nonmedical instructional staff counts, salary outlays, and weighted monthly salaries broken down by academic rank, gender, and contract length. Each row is uniquely identified by UNITID and academic rank (ARANK).

Counts and salary outlays for full-time nonmedical noninstructional staff, broken down by occupational category. The description does not provide a named row-key variable beyond the institution and occupational category.

Membership records for custom comparison groups submitted for the 2013 IPEDS Data Feedback Report, listing each comparison institution’s UNITID, name, and state. Rows represent a comparison institution within a submitted group, identified by the submitting institution and comparison institution.

Institution-level response-status records for each IPEDS survey component, including response, imputation, applicability, parent/child reporting, and revised-data indicators. Rows are identified by institution (UNITID) and survey component.

Institution directory records containing each institution’s name, location, contact and web links, active status, Title IV participation, and institutional classifications. The grain is one record per IPEDS institution (UNITID).

Institutional characteristics covering program and award-level offerings, control and affiliations, special learning opportunities, and admissions applicants, admits, and test scores. Admissions variables apply only to institutions without an open-admission policy; the grain is one institution (UNITID).

Student charges for full academic-year programs at institutions whose programs are primarily credit-hour based and use a semester, quarter, trimester, 4-1-4, or other academic calendar. The institution-level record includes undergraduate and graduate tuition and fees, part-time per-credit charges, professional-practice charges, and published full-time first-time undergraduate attendance costs; the grain is one institution (UNITID).

Student charges reported for the full length of vocational programs at institutions using clock hours or primarily occupational credit-hour programs. The institution-level record includes the number of programs, attendance costs for the largest program, and tuition, fees, and books and supplies for up to five additional programs; the grain is one institution (UNITID) and program.
Institution-level mission statement information, containing either the statement itself or its web address. The grain is one institution (UNITID).

Student financial-aid recipient counts and total and average aid amounts broken down by undergraduate population and aid source/type. The row grain is institution × population (full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates or all undergraduates) × aid category; aid categories include federal, Pell, other federal, state/local, institutional, and federal/nonfederal loans for the first-time cohort, and total grants, Pell grants, and federal loans for all undergraduates.

Average net price and the underlying financial-aid amounts for full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates in two separate cohorts: grant-and-scholarship recipients and Title IV federal-aid recipients. The row grain is institution × cohort × academic year for 2009-10, 2010-11, and 2011-12; at public institutions, both cohorts are restricted to students paying the in-district or in-state tuition rate.
